# v0.32.0

## Highlights

This release features 814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)!

* **Structured decisions and generic parsers**: the new `POST /v1/systemone` endpoint answers `choice`, `noul` and `score` questions over a structured state (#59299), is served by default (#60677, #60696), and also runs on `Cloudflare/clef-omni` (#61064), `LiquidAI/d1-3B` (#60676) and DiffusionGemma (#60466). The new `hf` tool and reasoning parser (`--tool-call-parser hf`, `--reasoning-parser hf`) reads the checkpoint's `response_template`, so models that ship it need no model-specific parser (#58604, #58602), in both the Python and Rust frontends (#59005).
* **Low-precision KV cache everywhere**: NVFP4 KV cache now runs on SM8x and SM12x (#46963), SM90 (#60620) and with XQA decode on SM12x (#60452), and on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on SM100 (#59300); GLM-5.x defaults to an FP8 KV cache on SM100, halving KV memory per rank with 2.3-5.5% more throughput at a 7-11% TTFT cost in the PR's benchmark (#60140, #60281); `fp8_ds_mla` on SM90 gives GLM-5.3-Flash up to 31% more output throughput (#59246); ROCm gains the 4-bit `ultraquant_4bit` KV cache with about 2x the density of FP8 (#57057).
* **Model Runner V2**: a GPU n-gram speculator with variable-length drafts (#40704), Elastic EP (#53934), pipeline parallelism with prefill context parallelism for MLA models (#59139), a stock torch.compile mode (#59079), and MRV2 is now the default on ROCm with the model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360).
* **Faster startup and serving**: `vllm download-kernels` installs FlashInfer's precompiled kernels (#58765); `vllm preload --preload-autotune` keeps the FlashInfer autotune table warm across restarts (#60085); a shared-memory tensor arena broadcasts large multimodal tensors to workers with one copy (#51207); tokenizers and processors load from the local snapshot (#60825); and with `--api-server-count` above 1 each connection goes to the least-loaded API worker, for 43-85% more req/s on short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, 32 input / 1 output tokens) in the PR's benchmark (#60723).
* **Model support**: new EmbeddingGemma 2 omni-modal embeddings (#60254), MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#58674) and Nemotron 3.5 ASR (#59827); video input in the Transformers modeling backend (#57441); GLM-5.3 sparse MLA index conversions reused across layers (3.5-3.9x on that kernel, #59464) and fused multi-step draft decode (13.3% at concurrency 1, #57443); HiSparse per-request residency caching for up to 58% more throughput on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200 with long, fully GPU-resident contexts at high concurrency (#60083).
* **Security**: fixes for GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7 (chat template resource exhaustion, #50300), GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4 (tokenizer `max_token_id`, #59491) and GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9 (P2P ZMQ socket exhaustion, #51504); CORS no longer allows every origin by default (#61009); untrusted images are limited to raster formats (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are signed (#59357); and JSON schemas nested deeper than 64 levels are rejected (#60036).
* **Breaking changes**: Python 3.10 dropped (#60402); default CORS origins restricted (#61009); `transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0` and `tokenizers>=0.23.2` (#57387, #59796); torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes removed (#60517); cascade attention removed (#61126); `mamba_cache_mode="all"` removed (#58997); `max_tokens` no longer reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API reasoning stream events renamed (#59652).

## Release Artifacts

### Python Wheels

| Platform | Install |
|---|---|
| PyPI (CUDA 13.0) | `pip install vllm` |
| PyPI (CUDA 13.0, uv) | `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto` |
| ROCm | `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.32.0/rocm723` |
| XPU | `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.32.0/xpu --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu --index-strategy unsafe-best-match` |

### Docker Images

| Platform | Docker Image |
|---|---|
| CUDA 13.0 (Default) | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0` |
| CUDA 12.9 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0-cu129` |
| CUDA 13.0 + Ubuntu 24.04 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0-ubuntu2404` |
| CUDA 12.9 + Ubuntu 24.04 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0-cu129-ubuntu2404` |
| ROCm | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0` |
| CPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.32.0` |
| XPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.32.0` |

### Other Artifacts

Pre-built release artifacts are available in the **Assets** section at the bottom of this page, including:
- Source distribution tarball
- CUDA 12.9 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64
- CUDA 13.0 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64
- CPU Python wheels for x86_64, arm64, and macOS
- XPU Python wheel for x86_64

## Model Support
* **New models**: EmbeddingGemma 2 (`google/embeddinggemma-2`), an omni-modal text/image/audio/video embedding model, with unused modality encoders skipped through `--limit-mm-per-prompt` (#60254, #60289); MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#58674); Nemotron 3.5 ASR (`nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b`) complete-audio transcription; native realtime streaming is not yet supported (#59827); `Cloudflare/clef-omni` (#61064) and `LiquidAI/d1-3B` (#60676) on `/v1/systemone`; PLaMo 3 reasoning and tool parsers (#56575); and the zerank-2 reranker score template (#60415).
* **Transformers modeling backend**: video inputs (#57441), and Glm, Arcee, CWM, Mellum (#59679), GPT-NeoX, Phi, Seed-OSS and Jais2 (#59701) now served through it.
* **New model capabilities**: LoRA for BERT, RoBERTa and XLM-RoBERTa embedding models (#61033); Granite as an EAGLE3/DFlash target (#60855); Qwen3-ASR EAGLE3 (#52824); Sarvam MLA EAGLE3/DSpark with PP (#55902); GLM-5.3-Flash with the DFlash2 drafter (#56983); and MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 at PP > 1 on MRV2 (#57197) with MTP sharing target embeddings under PP (#58648).
* **GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash**: sparse MLA index conversion reused across layers (#59464), fused multi-step draft decode (#57443), FP8 KV cache default on SM100 (#60140, #60281), `fp8_ds_mla` on SM90 (#59246), qlnorm skipped for MHA (4.4-7.7% TTFT, #58845), long-context indexer prefill sharded across TP (up to 25% lower TTFT at 1M context, #54951), DCP for the kpool indexer (#59211, #60032), KDA prefill checkpoints with FlashKDA (#56960), FP8 KV on SM90 sparse MLA (#55222), `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` honored for KDA state (#59147), a generic packed KV layout (#57169), MTP index sharing restored (#61079), and fixes for vision-tower crashes (#59126), non-square image encoder budgets (#59565), DP startup (#56974), video timestamps (#55647), DFlash2/EAGLE3 aux hidden states (#60763) and null-block writes (#59528).
* **DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1**: decoder-side SWA bounded replay (#58132) with replay layers in CUDA graphs and trimmed in PIECEWISE graphs (`compilation_config.decoder_replay_trim_threshold`, #59532) plus last KV-source layer trimming (+3.6%, #59894), packed FP8 Engram exchange across DP (#59923), faster CPU-offloaded Engram lookups (#59327), fused DeepSeek V4 + MTP drafting (#58463), encoder CUDA graph packing for V4.1 and Kimi-K3 (11% lower mean TTFT, #58925), EPLB for DSpark drafts (#57549), and fixes for NVFP4 checkpoints with 0% draft acceptance (#59655), MegaMoE shared-expert finalize ordering (#59927), worst-case vision dummy inputs (#57898, #59271), compressor ring null-block writes (#58560), Triton 3.9 indexer quantization (#60716) and decoder-replay CUDA graphs with FlashInfer EP MoE backends (#61041).
* **Qwen**: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp) merged QSA projections in one GEMM (1.45-1.68x, #59533), fused QSA pre-indexer (#57097), sequence parallelism through `--enable-hc-sp` (#56322), SM100 low-latency decode GEMM plans (up to 2.7x vs cuBLAS on small-M, #59214), `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` honored (#60023), and PLE loading for INC (#59990), Quark (#59443) and pre-SM89 GPUs (#60142); Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 M-RoPE cache 4x smaller and Qwen3.5 YaRN matching Transformers (#59853); Qwen3-Omni M-RoPE fixes (#58890, #59842); Qwen3-ASR on the upstream processor (#57146); Qwen3-VL unknown video fps (#60501) and per-video options with the multimodal cache (#55203).
* **Kimi-K3 and MiniMax-M3**: Kimi-K3 FlashInfer fused speculative KDA on SM100 (#54255), fused vision processor (10-20x preprocessing at 1080p-8K, #59278), fused K/V pack on the DCP prefill path (#56881), and DSpark KV cache back to 4 groups (#59733); MiniMax-M3 MSA prefill with an E4M3 query (26-37% faster with FP8 KV, #60684), FP8 indexer cache on non-SM100 GPUs (#59081), Triton indexer tuning (#56151, #59481), and indexer score fixes (#60194, #54597).
* **Multimodal**: device-side input normalization for Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5/Qwen4Exp (#51289), GLM-V and GLM-OCR (#55389), Llama Nemotron VL (#57928) and Kimi K2.5/K3 (#59278), kept fused under `compile_mm_encoder` (#59195); encoder inputs sorted by modality (6.5-8.2% more req/s, #60196); Mistral 3 preprocessing 8% faster (#57531); Pixtral `compile_mm_encoder` (#57168); and fixes for Llama 4 / Mistral Large 3 EAGLE drafters (regression since v0.28.0, #57633), Phi-4 MM audio OOM (#60614), DeepSeek-OCR zero-sum pixels (#59417), MiMo-V2.5/V2.6 with fastsafetensors (#58142), MiMo-V2.6 FP8 KV cache (#58128), Voxtral realtime (#45022), Nemotron Super vision LayerNorm (#61401), K-EXAONE config and MTP RoPE (#60187), Nemotron Parse tied `lm_head` (#60272), LongCat-Flash MTP loading (#60080) and Ling-3.0-flash-VL (#59026).

## Engine Core
* **Model Runner V2**: GPU n-gram speculator (#40704), Elastic EP with drain-then-commit scaling (#53934), PP with PCP for MLA models (#59139), `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE` mode (#59079), dynamic K in autoregressive speculators (#57053), MTP sampling-mask replay (#59359) and per-module LM heads (#58921), non-blocking H2D copies on WSL2 (#60215), and fixes for int64 index offsets at long context (#60736), warmup (#61013), GDN prefill checkpoints (#59536) and MRV2+PP+MTP align state (#60210).
* **Speculative decoding**: fused multi-step draft decode on FlashInfer trtllm-gen (#58371), FlashInfer ReplaySSM for Mamba2 MTP (#52928), in-graph metadata for DFlash/DSpark drafts (#60692), and correctness fixes for ngram on hybrid recurrent models (#56531), Mamba prefill checkpoints with MTP and prefix caching (#59759, #60797), stop-string trimming (#47616), draft model config (#61240), adaptive block verification (#60945), DSpark bonus slots (#59105) and draft models on the Transformers backend (#59293).
* **Hybrid models and prefix caching**: Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoints for NemotronH, Granite-4.0-H, Falcon-H1 and Zamba2 (#57329), stale block hashes dropped when streaming sessions truncate (#59103), and fixes for quantized Mamba-2 with TP (#58083), spec decode page sizes (#59975), prefix-cache bounds (#55601, #60533) and sm90 Mamba2 NaNs (#61718).
* **Sleep and RL**: sleep releases workspace scratch (up to 4.5 GiB/GPU, #59156) and KV-init state (about 4.6 GiB/GPU, #59158), opt-in `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` (#59160, #59523); token-level weight-version spans on outputs (#59582, #61070); weight-transfer communicators released without stopping inference (#61060); `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names 'draft.*'` (#61046); `modelexpress` weight-transfer backend (#58399); `POST /weight_checker` (#51350); weight-transfer metrics (#55781); `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` releasing the MNNVL workspace (#59360); and `sleep(level=2)` keeping FP8 KV scales (#57163).
* **HiSparse**: per-request residency cache (up to 58% at high concurrency with GPU-resident contexts, #60083), lower scheduler overhead (#57930), GPU residency owned by HiSparse (#60647), less staging memory (#60429), host cache gauges (#58949, #59485), and fixes for decode token limits (#60682) and TP hangs (#60941).
* **Startup and memory**: shared-memory tensor arena (`--enable-shm-tensor-arena`, on by default, #51207), Fast Start with PP (#55477), daemon-held weights counted against `gpu_memory_utilization` (#57298), autotune preload (#60085), local tokenizer snapshots (#60825), `sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor` saving several GiB at 1M context (#61023), cached memory reclaimed during weight loading (#57516), fewer Triton sampler warmup compiles (#58605), sharded state loader with PP (#52110), and `reload_weights` with Run:ai streamer (#58124).
* **Kernels and runtime**: MoE weighted-sum tuning (1.17-2.37x, #59731), flash-maxsim kernels for ColBERT/ColPali scoring (#40337), fallback detokenization with 69% less CPU at 32K tokens (#60497), faster KV block free queue (#60269), Triton kernels off `tl.make_block_ptr` (#60502), fusion passes restored under PyTorch 2.15 (#57299) and static FP8 quant fusion on recent torch (#61108).
* **Batch invariance**: custom all-reduce under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (#58623), deterministic split-K LoRA shrink (#59377), every attention backend checked (#60271), SM120 TP configs (#58495), and ROCm support (#52231).
* **Observability**: `vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_by_source_total` (#56318), `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage` (#58874), `vllm:admission_rejections_total` (#55812), `vllm:watermark_requests` (#58715), `--custom-histogram-buckets` (#48867), a JSON log formatter via `LoggingConfig.formatter` (#58739), and per-session profiling controls (#57875).

## Large Scale Serving
* **MoE communication**: FlashInfer CuteDSL MegaMoE for more models via `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` (#54049), FP8 combine for the FlashInfer one-sided all2all (+4% at DEP8, #57995), NCCL symmetric-memory MoE reduce-scatter (9.6-16% lower latency, #49194), DeepEPv2 hybrid NVLink+RDMA mode on by default (#57991), Kimi-K3 shared experts with DeepEP v2 (#56875), and opt-in EPLB migration batching (#52641).
* **Context parallelism**: decode requests sharded across PCP ranks (#52162) and TokenSpeed MLA with block-interleaved DCP for heterogeneous NIXL disaggregation (#59462).
* **KV connectors**: NIXL host-buffer copies coalesced (#54483), mixed block sizes (#58860), peer metadata recovery (#55471) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MTP acceptance in P/D (#59997); Mooncake coalesced hybrid/MLA RDMA regions (#57952) and bootstrap retries (#55923); MoRIIO Kimi-K3 DSpark READ (#57700); DeepSeek-V4.1 P/D skipping bounded replay for loaded KV (#59197); and KVCR pool-and-index API (#59899).
* **Data parallelism**: streaming requests pinned to their engine (#59017), per-engine RNG streams (#59788), and placement groups without `ray[default]` (#57648).

## Hardware & Performance
* **NVIDIA**: native 64-head FlashMLA sparse prefill on SM100 (1.16-1.18x TTFT, #60029), block-FP8 DeepGEMM experts skipping padding (#59128), SM120 split-K attention (#58482), DGX Spark Qwen4Exp GEMM plans (#59753, #59632, #60027), OAI Triton MXFP4 MoE on SM12x (#58877), and FlashInfer autotune cache per rank (#57635).
* **AMD ROCm**: DeepSeek-V4 AITER MegaMoEV2 via `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` (#59685) with opt-in shared-expert fusion (3-8%, #61004), opt-in mono decode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (`VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`, #60397), opt-in Gluon sparse MLA (up to +16% on GLM-5.2, #53492), paged MXFP4 indexer (#58671), opt-in a4w4 MoE for DSv4 (#58819), `ultraquant_4bit` KV cache (#57057), `aiter_flydsl` GDN prefill (#57560), Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoints (about 20% better TTFT, #58344), fused MLA decode (#57640) and per-rank latent MoE shards (#59591), GLM-5.3-Flash split-K sparse MLA decode (5-15% lower ITL, #58584), native `merge_attn_states` (2.4x, #60159), `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` for RDNA (#59132), gfx11 W4A16 tuning (up to 23% TTFT, #56301), MRV2 default with model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360), and fixes for sleep-mode segfaults on ROCm 7.2+ (#60367) and MLA weight reloads (#60389).
* **Intel XPU**: MLA in `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` (#58297), Arc Pro B70 FP8 GEMM (2.0-2.73x, #56063) and fused MoE configs (#53065), fused SYCL LayerNorm (#57172), and fixes for Gemma-2 softcap (#589

### Release readiness review (v0.23.1 -> TARGET 0f44a46474d1f37a6b0ee006251a78bde4179bea)

This is a release readiness report done by `$final-release-review` skill.

### Diff

https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/compare/v0.23.1...0f44a46474d1f37a6b0ee006251a78bde4179bea

### Release intent

- Review mode: final candidate, Release Please PR #5285.
- Intended release: minor, 0.24.0.
- Minimum required release type: minor. Existing tool error formatters receive a new category, and the RunState reader restricts some legacy agent identities.
- Versioning verdict: compatible with the required minor release.

### Release call

**🟢 GREEN LIGHT TO SHIP.** The prepared 0.24.0 candidate has no unresolved release blocker. Its compatibility changes have supported migration or fallback paths described below.

### Scope summary

- 111 files changed (+15,444/-1,412). Main areas: tool execution and failure recovery, durable RunState and session history, sandbox safety, tracing, examples, dependencies, and release metadata.
- The candidate contains current main and #5335. Changes beyond main are limited to release-owned metadata.

### Risk assessment (ordered by impact)

1. **Route affected saved runs to their original SDK and agent code.**
   - Risk: **🟢 LOW**, with a required upgrade precaution. Some previously readable checkpoints now fail safely instead of risking incorrect agent ownership.
   - Evidence: the writer advances from schema 1.18 to 1.21. The reader rejects certain older graphs with same-name non-root agents whose saved identity ordering could have depended on hook attributes, even when those attributes remained unchanged. New identity generation excludes all hook instance attributes and retains the hook type. Graphs distinguishable only by those attributes cannot be serialized. Other supported historical schemas remain readable.
   - Files: `src/agents/run_state.py`, `src/agents/_run_state_agent_identity.py`, `tests/test_run_state.py`.
   - Action: finish affected legacy tasks with the original SDK, unchanged agent definitions, and hook ordering used when the snapshot was written. Use unique agent names before starting new durable runs. Do not rename a stored graph or change its schema label to force migration. Older SDKs cannot read new 1.21 snapshots.

2. **Update existing custom tool error formatters for a third category.**
   - Risk: **🟢 LOW**, with an explicit migration for exhaustive callbacks. A formatter that treats every non-rejection as a missing tool can now return misleading text for a crashed function.
   - Evidence: `ToolErrorFormatterArgs.kind` adds `"tool_exception"`; the optional `error` field is appended. The run-wide callback now handles eligible decorated function failures. Explicit per-tool handlers, including explicit `None` or the default handler, keep precedence. Factory-created MCP and `Agent.as_tool` failures, timeouts, cancellation, and schema-backed program calls keep their separate behavior.
   - Files: `src/agents/run_config.py`, `src/agents/tool.py`, `src/agents/run_internal/tool_execution.py`, `tests/test_tool_exception_formatter.py`.
   - Action: handle `"tool_exception"` explicitly or return `None` for it to retain the default message. Keep exception details out of model-visible output unless deliberately sanitized. With no custom formatter, default behavior stays unchanged.

3. **Preserve completed work without promising automatic replay.**
   - Risk: **🟢 LOW**. Recovery retains more completed work, but applications must still reconcile external side effects and partially committed history.
   - Evidence: deferred approval history waits for the output guardrail boundary. For client-managed runs, accepted call/output pairs survive sibling or callback failures after input and tool-output guardrails permit publication. Server-managed conversations retain their separate recovery path. Pending writes retain session identity and compaction state. Automatic compaction waits for pending approvals; standalone Redis replacement uses a transaction. Conversations writes use batches of at most 20 items and can commit partially across requests.
   - Files: `src/agents/run_internal/session_persistence.py`, `src/agents/run_internal/tool_execution.py`, `src/agents/memory/openai_conversations_session.py`, `src/agents/memory/openai_responses_compaction_session.py`, `src/agents/extensions/memory/redis_session.py`.
   - Action: resume supported nonterminal failures with the original session backend and ID, us

# v0.31.0

## Highlights

This release features 717 commits from 307 contributors (96 new)!

* **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash performance**: FlashMLA mega attention with the V4.1 NVFP4 compressed KV cache is now the SM100 default (#56935); DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits for the indexer (#56254) and Mega-Gate fusing the gate GEMM with expert selection (#56266); decoder boundaries fuse the TP all-reduce, mHC input preparation (#57643) and the MoE finalize (#58586); a fused small-batch WO-A with inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant on SM100/SM103 (#58634); the MXFP8 `wo_b` GEMM fused with the sequence-parallel reduce-scatter (#57428); Engram `wkv` sharded across TP ranks (#58678) and Engram host tables shared across co-located DP replicas by default (#57651); encoder CUDA graphs for the vision tower (#56625); and SWA bounded replay that keeps the sliding-window KV out of prefix caching (#56227).
* **Fast restart**: the new `vllm preload` CLI launches the weight-cache daemon that keeps post-quantized weights resident in GPU memory across engine restarts (#56680), now with data parallelism (#57386), MTP draft models (#57312), a `/health` endpoint (#58552) and a readiness wait (#58370). Experimental initialized-engine snapshots (`vllm snapshot create/restore`) use CRIU to restore a fully initialized TP1 engine (#51360).
* **Model Runner V2 and speculative decoding**: draft-model speculative decoding (#43091) and custom logits processors (#56497) on Model Runner V2; the new LiLiCorr drafter (#57934); async scheduling for DFlash (#58065) with the context K/V precompute captured in the draft CUDA graph (#57632); DSpark adaptive verification for Gemma4 (#57263) and variable-length decode for Kimi-K3 (#52988); a DCP target with a non-DCP DSpark draft (#56723); and MoE memory now counted during MRV2 profiling, avoiding OOMs on WideEP deployments (#57270, #58411).
* **Large scale serving**: MoonEP balanced EP all2all backend via `--all2all-backend moonep` (#52101), prefill context parallelism with data parallelism (#57075), a low-SM multimem reduce-scatter for SM100/SM103 (#55072), DeepEPv2 with sequence parallelism (#57210) and EPLB with shared-expert overlap (#57236), a sharding-aware NCCL M2N weight-transfer backend for RL (#51520), and KV offloading back-pressure detection (#50045).
* **Scheduling controls**: `--max-num-active-seqs` caps RUNNING admission independently of `max_num_seqs` (#56758), `--long-prefill-token-threshold` now adapts to the number of waiting prefills instead of chunking a lone request (#57951, #58459), the waiting queue was reworked so requests already holding KV blocks are scheduled first (#58947), and the KV connector + MTP deadlock under KV pressure was fixed (#57104).
* **HiSparse hardening**: MTP verification rows resolved with a union residency kernel (#59235), MTP acceptance collapse under FULL graphs fixed (#59309), no GPU pages without host backing (#59036), a chunked-prefill preemption livelock fixed (#59494), KV cache sized from the groups HiSparse allocates (#59450), and host prefix publication and GPU prefix adoption fixes (#59007, #59282).
* **Security**: per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` are rejected unless `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` is set (#58830); prefix-cache extra keys are tagged by source so a LoRA name and a `cache_salt` can no longer collide (#51899), and the LoRA path is part of the block hash (#59335); stale multimodal receiver-cache entries can no longer replace fresh payloads (#57833).
* **Breaking changes**: per-request multimodal kwargs gated (#58830); `tokenizer_mode="slow"` removed (#58545); `--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` renamed to `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` (#57382); online quantization through `quantization="fp8"` replaced by the `fp8_per_tensor` shorthand (#53585) and Quark silent online quantization removed (#51800); the AllSpark INT8 W8A16 backend removed (#58001); `--enforce-eager` now also disables JIT kernel warmup (#58197); XPU graphs enabled by default with `VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH` removed (#51600).

## Release Artifacts

### Python Wheels

| Platform | Install |
|---|---|
| PyPI (CUDA 13.0) | `pip install vllm` |
| PyPI (CUDA 13.0, uv) | `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto` |
| ROCm | `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.31.0/rocm723` |
| XPU | `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.31.0/xpu --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu --index-strategy unsafe-best-match` |

### Docker Images

| Platform | Docker Image |
|---|---|
| CUDA 13.0 (Default) | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` |
| CUDA 12.9 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0-cu129` |
| ROCm | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.31.0` |
| CPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.31.0` |
| XPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.31.0` |

### Other Artifacts

Pre-built release artifacts are available in the **Assets** section at the bottom of this page, including:
- Source distribution tarball
- CUDA 12.9 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64
- CUDA 13.0 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64
- CPU Python wheels for x86_64, arm64, and macOS
- XPU Python wheel for x86_64

## Model Support
* **New model capabilities**: DiffusionGemma structured generation mode with bounded single-token choices (#57250), MiMo V2 MXFP4 MoE, BF16 MoE router and DFlash drafts (#57784), Cohere2MoE auxiliary hidden states for EAGLE3/DFlash drafters (#49819), GLM-5.2-MXFP4 on the ROCm DeepSeek-V3.2 path (#51915), AMD-Quark mixed-precision DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4 (#57071) and GLM-5.3-Flash Quark MXFP4 (#56176) checkpoints, and a built-in `granite_thinking_parser` for Granite 4.2 (#55957).
* **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**: FlashMLA mega attention with the NVFP4 compressed KV cache as the SM100 default (#56935), DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits in the indexer (#56254), Mega-Gate (#56266), fused TP all-reduce + mHC input preparation (#57643) with the MoE finalize folded in (#58586), fused small-batch WO-A (#58634), MXFP8 `wo_b` GEMM + reduce-scatter (#57428), overlapped mHC coefficients for small TP batches (#57603) limited to FULL CUDA graphs (#57874), Engram `wkv` sharded across TP (#58678), serialized Engram lookups with huge-page host tables (#56926), Engram tables shared across DP replicas by default (#57651, #57914, #59068), native shared-expert MegaMoE fusion without padding (#56568, #57204), faster MegaMoE staging and NVFP4 cache gathers (#57604), the fused query RMSNorm + MXFP8 path restored (#57679), KV-only DSpark context insertion (#56441), vision encoder CUDA graphs (#56625, #58499), SWA bounded replay (#56227), causal image SWA restored to match the reference (#57152), updated reasoning effort mappings (#58316), and startup fixes for NaN-scored candidate blocks (#57454), DeepSelect sentinels (#58215), DSpark non-causal attention on FlashInfer (#57432), runtime JIT of offset candidate buffers (#57667) and imports without Triton (#57654).
* **DeepSeek V4**: FlashInfer sparse MLA with fused inverse RoPE + FP8 quant (#58621), stacked DSpark context WKV projections (#54674), fused MoE expert distribution computed from the EP group (#57465), FIM completion via `suffix` (#44229), missing `string=` in tool calls parsed (#56271), request tools attached to an existing system message (#51856), image block spacing preserved (#56882), and DSpark width separated from MTP stage validation (#54631).
* **GLM-5.3-Flash**: opt-in FlashAttention and FlashMLA sparse backends on SM90 (#55385), NoPE sparse MLA on the FlashInfer SM120 backend (#55277), cooperative top-k for small decode batches (#57327), indexer decode workspace sized by pooled length (3 GiB saved, #57701), metadata ops 1.6-4.8x faster (#58450), fused kpool tail slot mapping (#57534), kpool top-k through the shared dispatcher (#57546), lower sparse MLA preparation overhead (#57458), no D2H sync in the SM90 sparse MLA plan under async scheduling (#58684), FlashKDA keeping the recurrent state in FP32 for long prefills (#58846), and correctness fixes for kpool corruption with speculative decoding (#58454), SM90 `index_kpool` mismatch (#58704), kpool tail strides (#57477), 500k-token prompts (#57317), dense MLP layers under sequence parallelism (#58061), indexer top-k backend selection (#58594) and varlen paged MQA launches (#55270).
* **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp)**: FP8 main KV cache on the QSA path (#55557), FP8 TP with FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE (#55867), SM90 QSA tuning (#57273), fused HC down projection + SiLU (#58957), lower PLE metadata overhead (#58114), QSA indexer workspace fragmentation fixed (#57105), profiling KV cache released (#58961), pinned PLE prefetch ids kept out of the CUDA graph pool (#58489), and indexed expert-mapping lookups saving about 25 s of weight loading on DGX Spark (#58720).
* **Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3**: Kimi-K3 vision patch embedder as a GEMM (#58527), fused KimiViT QK RoPE (up to 29x, #58651), routed expert quantization (#57430), reasoning parser (#57098) and reasoning token counting (#58372) fixes, DSpark context KV pointers refreshed after re-binding (#58814), stateless first chunks no longer classified as decodes (#51483), and Mamba block estimates that no longer stall admission on external prefix hits (#57050); MiniMax-M3 encoder CUDA graphs (#58673), `Conv3dLayer` patch embedding (about 62x, #58512), `triton_mrope` in the vision tower (#58526), fused MiniMax2 routing with non-unit scaling (#58880), and processor fixes (#58460, #59613).
* **DiffusionGemma**: one-pass sampler statistics kernel (#58226), `diffusion_constrained` reads over `logprob_token_ids` (about 25% faster, #58216), fewer logit rows for prefill-only batches (#57416), `logprob_token_ids` support (#57417), and fixes for concurrent logprobs (#57414), eager fallback dtype (#57462), multimodal inputs (#57589), quantized LM heads (#48521) and CPU execution (#58964).
* **Multimodal**: Triton `mm_input_norm` kernel (#56798, #56711), raw pixels kept through the DP-sharded ViT path (#56872), Qwen2.5-VL video fps honored for temporal M-RoPE (#47736), Whisper and Qwen2-Audio clips longer than 30s (#57769, #56912), Mistral3 placeholder grid (#53758), Idefics3 unsplit patches (#48760), Ovis2.5 tokens (#52623), Aria expert weights (#57487), MiMo-V2.5 fused FP8 `qkv_proj` sharding (#57508), Gemma4 `AutoWeightsLoader` (#55911) and buffer scalars (#54213), Gemma4 FP8 KV with FA4 at head dim 512 (#53175), Laguna RoPE (#57189), Mistral-Large-3 accuracy regression (#57563), malformed EXIF (#56527, #57234), JinaVL labels (#57347), Sarvam MLA routing with FP32 router logits (#56034), fused CohereASR attention scores (#55190), and fused DFlash2 grouped convolution (#55960).
* **LoRA**: Nemotron VL language models (#56231), ModernBert (#57148), VoyageQwen3 embeddings (#57708), RoBERTa sequence classification (#58884), and `modules_to_save` sequence-classification heads (#53555) with per-adapter `num_labels` (#57766).

## Engine Core
* **Model Runner V2**: draft-model speculative decoding (#43091), custom logits processors (#56497) validated at admission (#57728), randomized dummy inputs (#58411), dummy tokens routed to MoE experts during profiling (#57270), FULL decode graphs for one-token prompt tails (#58400), token-to-request mappings shared (#57102) and Mamba/GDN metadata reused across KV cache groups (#58762), encoder-only ViT CUDA graphs (#56922), weight offloader (#57834) and pooling model (#57737) released on shutdown, and fixes for multi-layer MTP KV in P/D (#55055), fast-prefill with LoRA (#56456), stale block-table writes from dummy draft steps (#56734), padded prompt tails in hybrid models (#58434), never-proposed draft slots (#58784), auto-fit `max_model_len` (#58149) and `intermediate_tensors` during capture (#57745).
* **Speculative decoding**: LiLiCorr drafter (#57934), DFlash async scheduling (#58065) and context K/V in the draft CUDA graph (#57632), Gemma4 DSpark adaptive verification (#57263), Kimi-K3 variable-length adaptive verification (#52988), CPU-GPU sync removed for heterogeneous vocabularies (#57396), Triton recompiles avoided in the acceptance estimator (#57107), and fixes for EAGLE/dense drafts with EP (#56930), DFlash/DSpark profiling batches (#56448), GLM MTP head memory (#55442), prompt embeddings with drafts (#57356), and TritonMLA causal multi-token decode (#51065).
* **Scheduler**: `--max-num-active-seqs` (#56758), adaptive `--long-prefill-token-threshold` (#57951, #58459), `skipped_waiting` replaced by a KV-holding waiting queue (#58947), atomic admission of `n > 1` requests (#53936), KV connector + MTP deadlock (#57104), a throughput cliff when `max_num_seqs` is not a multiple of 8 (#57355), streaming continuations keeping logprobs and refreshing max tokens (#57447, #57676), a resumable request + async scheduling race (#58259), and a non-blocking structured-output grammar poll (#55931).
* **Prefix caching and hybrid models**: extra keys tagged by source (#51899) and LoRA paths hashed (#59335), `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` (#57382), prompt-tail hits with MTP restored (#58368), prompt-end checkpoints kept under sparse retention (#59146), align-mode checkpoint reservation (#59175), stateless GDN first chunks (#51565), MTP draft KV cache groups annotated on the hybrid grouping path (#55390), a generalized prefill checkpoint builder (#57783), batched Mamba2 prefill state saves without GPU-CPU syncs (#49371), `skip_reading_prefix_cache` honored for connector hits (#57269), incremental multimodal block hashing (#51694), a KV block size every attention backend supports (#49845) with clearer errors (#58557), and `CacheConfig.effective_attention_block_size` for DCP (#56538).
* **Startup and memory**: parallel Triton warmup compilation (#58582), JIT warmup disabled under `--enforce-eager` (#58197) unless fault tolerance is on (#58593), DeepGEMM warmup reusing the MoE workspace (#57268), allocator fragmentation no longer shrinking the KV cache during profiling (#58430), sparse prefill buffers reserved before KV sizing (#57575), stale FlashMLA workspace views released (#56902), DeepGEMM FP8 workspace halved (#53914), shared Marlin/Humming workspaces (#57421), FlashInfer BF16 MoE weights converted in place (#54699), UniProc startup threads bounded by the CPU quota (#58946), and runtime threads set before profiling (#55891).
* **Kernels**: sampled filtering for persistent top-k (#56346), Murmur3 RNG for Gumbel sampling (#51367), register-resident per-token-group 8-bit quant (#55330), vectorized per-tensor FP8 abs-max (#58194), a Triton kernel dispatcher for platform-specific overrides (#43048), `GateLinear` for all MoE models (#58234), non-local expert slots skipped in `TritonExperts` (#58051), deferred TRT-LLM-Gen top-k finalize on the modular path (#58635), SM120 batch-invariant matmul configs (#57456), FlashInfer prefill dequant scratch bounded (#57918), and fixes for Triton softcap NaNs (#56579), QuIP Hadamard transforms (#43462), CUTLASS FP8 linear on A100 (#55884), FlashInfer sampling on unsupported GPUs (#48956), SM100 FP8 blockwise scale padding (#57377), mixed FULL graph prefill capture (#58275) Inductor custom-op pattern matching (#58189), CuteDSL BF16 GDN prefill diverging from FLA on Qwen3.5 (#53864), SM100 `fp8_ds_mla` cache scales (#49435), ragged decode batches in the sparse indexer (#52500), stale `allowed_token_ids` masks after batch reordering (#48419, #43931), and `prompt_embeds` tensors held after requests finish (#57988).
* **Batch invariance**: breakable CUDA graphs without torch.compile by default under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (#57586), sequence parallelism and async TP disabled (#56377), and NCCL 2.31 collectives kept enabled (#58179).
* **Sleep and RL**: `release_kv_cache_memory()` frees only KV cache memory (#44890), `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names` retains frozen weights across level-2 sleep (#57891), NCCL M2N weight transfer (#51520), dense DP weight

*779 PRs from 227 contributors.*

## New models

| Model | Type | Cookbook |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4_1) |
| GigaChat 3.5 | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/GigaChat/GigaChat3.5) |
| IQuest-Q1 | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/IQuestLab/IQuest-Q1) |
| MiMo-V2.6 / MiMo-V2.6-Pro | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Xiaomi/MiMo-V2.6) |
| Ling-3.0-flash-VL | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/InclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL) |
| DiffusionGemma | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Google/DiffusionGemma) |
| Qwen-Image 2.1 | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/Qwen-Image/Qwen-Image-2.1) |
| Anima Base v1.0 | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/CircleStone/Anima) |
| Ming-Image 0.1 Design / Design-Layer | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/inclusionAI/Ming-Image) |
| FLUX 3 Action | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/vla/FLUX/FLUX-3-Action) |

## Key features

* PD instances can switch between prefill and decode on the fly, no restart needed ([#28403](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28403)).
* The prefix cache now runs on a Rust core by default ([#39627](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39627)).
* DeepSeek-V4.1 gets 22% faster first token on long prompts ([#40352](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40352)).
* Kimi K3 gets 20.6% higher prefill throughput in PD serving ([#40045](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40045)).
* GLM-5.3-Flash now runs on AMD MI355X, with FP8 / MXFP4 MoE and MTP speculative decoding ([#38546](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38546), [#39341](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39341), [#39778](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39778)).
* More accurate results under PP, DP attention, and CP, with layer communication now handled by SGLang ([guide](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/developer_guide/layer_boundary), [#41557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41557)).
* New Decisions API (`/v1/decisions`) turns an LLM / VLM into a low-latency classifier and scorer ([docs](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/supported-models/decision_models), [#41208](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41208)).
* Score API (`/v1/score`) scores all candidates in one request ([#38965](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38965), [#41188](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41188)).
* Run MiniMax-H3 with SGLang Diffusion inside ComfyUI ([#35990](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35990)).

## To upgrade

```bash
uv pip install --prerelease=allow sglang==0.5.21
```

items.briefingSourceText: Observability & Evals LangSmith What Is Eval-Driven Development? How to Improve AI Agents Divya Santhanam November 9, 2026 12 min Go back to blog Create agents Create agents Share Key Takeaways Eval-driven development (EDD) involves building an agent while measuring performance against a consistent set of metrics and hill climbing toward an eval. The first step of EDD is to create a short spec of what good looks like for your desired behavior. Include what the agent shouldn't do and what has to keep working. As you iterate, judge a change you make to the agent by comparing experiments. A change that fixes one case may break another. Keep evals running in CI and in production, and turn the failures you find into new dataset examples. Development on most agents starts the same way. You write a prompt, try a few questions by hand, adjust, and try again. This works well in the beginning, when agent errors are obvious and improvements are easy to see. But over time it becomes increasingly difficult to know whether your most recent change made an agent better or worse. Eval-driven development (EDD) solves this by giving you a consistent set of metrics to measure your agent’s performance against and guide your decision making. Here at LangChain we've used EDD when building our most advanced agents (check out our blog on IssueBench ), and have boiled it down to a three step process: Define what good looks like for your agent. Write the eval before you build. Make your change and compare. In this blog, we'll walk through this process step by step so that your team can apply it to your own agent development process. What is eval-driven development? The name and concept of eval-driven development borrows from test-driven development (TDD), where you write a failing test before writing the code that passes it. Agents differ from traditional code as they're non-deterministic: Outputs vary. The same question can receive a different answer on each run. More than one answer can be right. Two natural language results can both be considered correct despite using different phrasing. The agent chooses its own steps. It might call a tool it didn't need, or skip one it should have used, and still reach the correct answer. As a result, agents need a different kind of test. An eval handles this by scoring runs of your agent across a set of examples. Evals are more flexible than traditional testing. You can score any aspect of the agent's run and you can use other LLMs to score it ( LLM-as-a-judge ). With EDD, similar to TDD, these evals become your definition of success and you build your agent towards them. Step 1: Define what good looks like for your agent The first step in EDD is defining what your agent should do. Then, list the behaviors it needs to handle to get there. These could be tasks such as answering questions from a knowledge base, taking an action on a user's behalf, or knowing when to ask a follow-up question. Write down the requirements for each behavior. Together, these make up a product requirements document (PRD) for your agent. EDD works on one behavior at a time. This gives you a narrow target to hill climb toward, without one change muddying the effect of another. The behavior you pick usually comes from a feature you're about to build or a failure you found in your agent's past runs. Before writing code, it’s helpful to define a short spec that covers: When the behavior should happen What the agent should do What the agent shouldn't do Which behaviors from your PRD must keep working The spec should be definitive enough to score as a pass or fail. Say we have an internal docs agent that employees query for company information. It has two tools: search_docs for internal documentation and web_search for everything else. We plan to add a create_ticket tool so it can file IT tickets. Our spec looks like this: When: A user reports something broken, like "My laptop won't connect to the VPN." Do: Call create_ticket . Don't: File a ticket for how-to questions, like “How do I connect to the VPN?” Keep intact: search_docs and web_search still handle the questions they handle today We’ll evaluate on these guidelines, even though the agent doesn’t have the capability yet. The current docs agent example implementation, plus the ticketing tool we plan to add. Each tool has an example input that would invoke it. Step 2: Write the eval before you build Build a dataset. A dataset is a collection of test cases (called “examples”) that have inputs and, optionally, reference “golden” outputs. One of the best sources for inputs is real agent runs. Users can phrase things in ways you wouldn't predict, and their requests include edge cases you may not think to write yourself. If your examples look like real traffic, a good score on your eval is more likely to mean good behavior in production. In LangSmith , you can directly add real agent runs to a dataset. If you don’t have any runs yet, a common alternative is to build your examples from scratch. For our docs agent, a handful of examples is enough to start. In our dataset, we’ll include ticket requests, plus questions that should still go to search_docs and web_search so existing behavior is accounted for. Each example pairs an input question with the reference output, the tool the agent should call. You can also extend your dataset to cover cases it doesn't have yet. Say we don't have many examples of frustrated users. We could give our existing examples to an LLM, ask it to rewrite them as angrier messages, and check that the agent still calls the right tool. Write an evaluator. Once you have your dataset, you can take your definition of "good" from your PRD and turn that into a test or eval that scores your agent’s performance on your examples. items.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

items.abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems rather than as a standalone model operating within a single context. Recent agent harnesses allow the model to instantiate worker agents and to author the executable workflow that coordinates them, shifting the design of system structure from developers to the model at run time. The quality of this organization therefore constitutes a distinct capability, yet existing benchmarks either measure end-to-end task completion or evaluate coordination under structures specified in advance. We formalize this capability as workflow orchestration and introduce WorkflowArena, a benchmark of 145 long-horizon tasks spanning 8 professional domains, from software engineering and formal mathematics to legal analysis and 3D production. Each task specifies an initial workspace and an integrated deliverable composed of interdependent components, which is assessed by a hidden verifier. Agents determine autonomously whether and how to delegate, and all delegation is recorded, enabling joint evaluation of deliverable quality and the organization of the underlying work. Experiments with nine models show that no single configuration performs best across all domains and that systems exhibit distinct delegation strategies: at high effort, Claude models in Claude Code invoke workflows less frequently but with larger worker groups, whereas GPT models in Codex delegate more frequently in smaller units. When the executing model is held fixed on a challenging subset of tasks, workflows authored by Claude Opus 5.5 substantially improve weaker executors, indicating that workflow organization is itself a measurable determinant of task performance.

items.whatChanged: WorkflowArena benchmark shows no single model configuration dominates across all professional domains, revealing distinct delegation strategies like Claude Code's low-frequency but large-group worker usage.
items.whyItMatters: Test the assumption that a universal agent orchestration strategy exists; consider domain-specific workflow templates rather than one-size-fits-all delegation logic.
items.evidenceQuote: Experiments with nine models show that no single configuration performs best across all domains
items.limitations: Results apply to 145 tasks in 8 domains; does not prove superiority for specific use cases or long-term stability.

items.whatChanged: Eval-driven development (EDD) proposes building agents by measuring performance against consistent metrics and hill-climbing toward those evals in CI and production.
items.whyItMatters: Implement a CI pipeline that runs fixed evals to objectively judge agent changes, replacing manual testing for ambiguous improvements.
items.evidenceQuote: Eval-driven development (EDD) involves building an agent while measuring performance against a consistent set of metrics
items.limitations: Source describes the methodology but does not provide empirical results on its effectiveness compared to traditional development.

items.whatChanged: Meta launched Muse Ember, a model priced at $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens, significantly cheaper than Claude Fable 5.2 at $8/$40.
items.whyItMatters: Evaluate whether Muse Ember can replace Fable 5.2 for high-volume, complex reasoning tasks where cost-per-token is the primary constraint.
items.evidenceQuote: For shorter prompts it's priced the same as GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 - both are $0.10/million input tokens and $0.50/million output
items.limitations: Pricing applies only to shorter prompts; token usage variance for reasoning tasks makes direct cost comparison unreliable without benchmark data.
